newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank starts re-discount business.
newsitem.headline: China central bank starts re-discount business.

text.p: The head office of the People's Bank of China has started to do re-discount business with the head offices of the four major state banks for the first time, the Shanghai Securities News said on Wednesday.

Since March 1, the central bank has been buying discount papers, which have yet to reach maturity, in the hands of the major state bank branches at a re-discount rate as a means of controlling money supply, the newspaper said.

The discount papers are commercial papers bought from state firms or enterprises at a discount rate by the four major state banks -- the Bank of China, the Construction Bank, the Agricultural Bank and the Industrial and Commercial Bank.
China's money supply is mainly controlled at present through annual loan quotas from the central bank to the four big banks, which account for around 75 percent of money supply in China.
The central bank has allowed its branches to do re-discount business with branches of the big four banks since 1994, but the headquarters of the banks have never before been involved.

"The central bank headquarters can use floating re-discount rates to influence the quantity of loans supplied by the major state banks and market interest rates," the newspaper said. "This in turn can help it to adjust money supply at the national level."

The central bank will each year decide an annual re-discount business volume between its head office and other banks' head offices to give it an effective means of controlling money supply, the newspaper said.

The volume of the re-discount business conducted by the head office of any one of the major state banks with the central bank head office must not exceed half of the discount papers in its hands, it said.
The banks must supply certificates to prove the quantity of their discount papers before they can do the business, it said.
Analysts said the major banks wanted to on-sell as much of the discount papers to the central bank as possible to make their assets more liquid.
The central bank will also select discount papers involving firms in pillar industries to be targets of re-discount business to support key industrial sectors, the newspaper said.
"This will help the central government to indicate its policy priorities towards selected industrial sectors and promote the services by major state banks in key industries," it added.
